mechanism_narrative: A sustained month-over-month increase in nonfarm employment (PAYEMS) indicates strengthening labor market conditions that directly boost consumer spending and corporate earnings, producing positive S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 trading days without regime dependence.
failure_condition: SPX 20d returns are negative in more than 55% of months with PAYEMS growth exceeding 0.5% MoM.

mechanism_narrative: When the unemployment rate (UNRATE) falls below 5.0%, it signals a tight labor market that accelerates consumer spending and corporate revenue growth, driving positive S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: In periods with UNRATE below 5.0%, SPX 20d returns are negative in more than 55% of cases.

mechanism_narrative: Concurrent increases in industrial production (INDPRO) and housing starts (HOUST) indicate synchronized expansion across manufacturing and construction sectors, which typically precedes stronger corporate profits and positive S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: When INDPRO and HOUST both increase, SPX 20d returns are negative in more than 55% of such instances.

mechanism_narrative: In a monetary tightening cycle defined by a sustained 3-month rise in the federal funds rate (FEDFUNDS) above 0.5%, the market anticipates reduced liquidity and higher borrowing costs, resulting in negative S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: In periods with FEDFUNDS rising > 0.5% in 3 months, SPX 20d returns are positive in more than 55% of cases.

mechanism_narrative: A year-over-year increase in the Consumer Price Index (CPIAUCSL) above 2.0% signals accelerating inflation that triggers Federal Reserve tightening expectations, leading to negative S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: When CPIAUCSL rises > 2.0% YoY, SPX 20d returns are positive in more than 55% of cases.

mechanism_narrative: Simultaneous growth in retail sales (RSAFS) and housing starts (HOUST) reflects robust consumer and housing demand, which supports economic expansion and corporate revenue growth, driving positive S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: When RSAFS and HOUST both increase, SPX 20d returns are negative in more than 55% of such instances.

mechanism_narrative: A month-over-month increase in industrial production (INDPRO) above 0.5% indicates expanding manufacturing output that correlates with rising corporate profits, producing positive S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: When INDPRO rises > 0.5% MoM, SPX 20d returns are negative in more than 55% of cases.

mechanism_narrative: A sustained month-over-month increase in nonfarm employment (PAYEMS) over a 60-day horizon indicates a strengthening labor market that supports long-term economic growth, driving positive S&P 500 forward returns over the next 60 trading days.
failure_condition: SPX 60d returns are negative in more than 55% of months with PAYEMS growth exceeding 0.5% MoM.
